title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary

This document is the canonical People Ops handbook for working at Redwood Inference. It covers: company culture and expectations, role definitions and career ladders, benefits & perks, hiring and onboarding overview, and an overview of core internal tools for new hires and managers. Use this as the first stop for employee-facing information; operational-runbooks and team-specific procedures will be linked where appropriate.

## 1. Introduction and Company Values

Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on shipping reliable, cost-optimized inference infrastructure. Our core values guide hiring, performance conversations, and day-to-day behavior:

- Customer-obsessed: prioritize reliability, latency, and developer experience for our customers.
- Clear ownership: teams own services end-to-end (build, deploy, operate).
- Measured impact: focus on measurable outcomes (SLOs, cost per request, adoption).
- Respectful candor: give and welcome feedback early and often.
- Continuous learning: experiments, postmortems, and knowledge sharing.

## 2. Roles and Career Ladders (high-level)

This section summarizes role families and career ladder expectations. Detailed leveling rubrics are maintained by People Ops and each manager.

Role families: engineering (infra, serving-runtime, platform, SRE), product, research/applied ML, developer experience, sales, customer success, people ops, finance/legal, security.

Career ladder structure (applies consistently across most IC families):

1. Associate / New Grad (IC1)
   - Learning-focused, executes defined tasks, requires mentorship.
2. Software Engineer / IC2
   - Delivers components, owns small features, writes tests and docs.
3. Senior Engineer / IC3
   - Leads features, designs subsystems, mentors others, influences roadmap.
4. Staff / IC4
   - Cross-team technical leadership, owns architecture decisions, drives major initiatives.
5. Principal / IC5+
   - Company-level strategy, multi-year technical roadmaps, recognized subject-matter expert.

Manager path: Manager, Senior Manager, Director, Senior Director, VP. Managers are evaluated on team outcomes (quality, velocity, hiring, retention) and people development.

Compensation bands and leveling: People Ops publishes band ranges in the compensation playbook (linked). Managers should discuss leveling during offers and performance cycles; refer compensation questions to People Ops.

## 3. Manager and IC Responsibilities

Manager responsibilities (summary):
- Hire, onboard, and retain top talent.
- Conduct regular 1:1s and career conversations.
- Set team goals tied to product metrics and SLOs.
- Run performance calibration and feedback cycles in collaboration with People Ops.

IC expectations (summary):
- Deliver reliable code and clear documentation.
- Participate in on-call rotations where applicable.
- Report incidents promptly and contribute to postmortems.
- Mentor peers and contribute to hiring.

## 4. Benefits & Perks (overview)

Redwood provides a competitive benefits package designed to support wellbeing, family needs, and professional growth. Key highlights: 

- Health: medical, dental, and vision coverage with multiple plan options; employer-paid basic life and AD&D.
- Financial: 401(k) with company match up to the stated policy, equity grants for full-time employees, and regular calibration for competitive salaries.
- Time off: flexible PTO policy (manager-approved), 10 paid company holidays, parental leave per local policy, and caregiver leave.
- Professional development: $2,000 annual learning stipend, internal training days, conference budget with manager approval.
- Remote and co-located work: hybrid-first policy with stipend for home office; relocation support for role-dependent hires.
- Wellness: monthly wellness stipend, annual mental health days, Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

How to enroll and manage benefits:
1. New hires receive a benefits enrollment email from People Ops on day 1.
2. Use the benefits portal (Workday/ADP dependent on location) to enroll within the first 30 days.
3. Questions about coverage, claims, or leaves should be routed to benefits@redwood.com.

## 5. Hiring and Interviewing Overview

Redwood follows a structured, candidate-friendly hiring process balancing speed and rigor. Hiring teams are responsible for following the interview loop and scoring rubric.

High-level process:
1. Requisition approval (hiring manager + finance + People Ops).
2. Draft job description and leveling recommendation.
3. Sourcing and outreach.
4. Screens: phone screen + technical/role-specific screens.
5. Onsite / virtual loop with cross-functional representation (coding/design/paired work + manager interview + bar-raiser).
6. Debrief and calibration with hiring panel.
7. Offer approval and compensation recommendation by People Ops.
8. Offer extension and negotiation.

Interview best practices and compliance:
- Use standardized rubrics (technical, culture, communication).
- Remove identifying info for take-home tests where bias reduction is requested.
- Ensure accessibility accommodations are offered proactively.

Hiring manager checklist (numbered):
1. Get role approved and matched to a band.
2. Coordinate interviews and select panelists (include at least one person outside the immediate team).
3. Share scoring rubric and candidate materials before interviews.
4. Consolidate feedback within 48 hours of the final interview.
5. Work with People Ops to finalize compensation and extend offer.

## 6. Onboarding: First 90 Days (playbook)

Goal: ensure new hires become productive, connected, and confident in Redwood primitives.

Pre-boarding (before day 1):
- Equipment shipped and access requested (IT ticket).
- Account provisioning (Google Workspace, Slack, Jira, internal tools) queued by People Ops and IT.
- Welcome packet with team context, first-week schedule, and reading list.

First week (orientation):
- Day 1: HR orientation, benefits overview, security training, meet manager 1:1.
- Days 2-5: Team onboarding, environment setup (repo access, local dev setup), "buddy" intro, and first small task.

30-day goals:
- Complete required trainings (security, compliance).
- Ship first small PR or documentation update.
- Regular 1:1 cadence established.

60-day goals:
- Take ownership of a medium-sized task and present a short readout.
- Participate in design discussions and code reviews.

90-day goals:
- Fully independent on core workflows; start a personal development plan with manager.
- Contribute to hiring or mentoring activities.

Onboarding checklist (quick):
- [ ] Equipment received and verified
- [ ] Access to SSO services (Slack, Google, Jira)
- [ ] Dev environment running and tests passing locally
- [ ] Completed security & compliance trainings
- [ ] 1:1 schedule with manager and buddy set

## 7. Internal Tools Guide (core systems & quick links)

This section lists the core internal tools every employee should know, with brief purpose and first-steps. Team-specific tools are documented on team-wide Confluence pages.

- Slack (primary communication): channels by team and product. Join #all-hands and your team channel. Use slash commands for status.
- Google Workspace (docs, calendar): calendar invites use business hours and timezone support.
- Jira (issue tracking): projects for product, infra, and SRE. Create tickets with components and priority tags.
- GitHub (code hosting): org-level repos. PR policy: require 1 approver for minor changes, 2 approvers for production changes. Use CODEOWNERS for critical services.
- CI/CD (CircleCI/GitHub Actions): builds trigger on PR; protected branches require passing checks.
- Internal console (service dashboards): access via SSO; includes cost dashboards, SLO panels, and alerting.
- On-call tooling (PagerDuty): on-call schedules, escalation policies, and runbooks linked in incident channel.
- HR portal (Workday/ADP): benefits, time-off, payroll.

Quick-start commands and examples:
- Git clone template repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-template.git
- Run local server (example): make dev && ./scripts/start_local.sh
- Open dashboards: https://console.redwood.internal (SSO required)

Security & access notes:
- Use SSO and MFA for all accounts.
- Access to production systems requires approved runbook and manager sign-off.
- Secrets are stored in the company vault; do not check credentials into code.

## 8. Performance Reviews and Growth

Cadence: bi-annual performance cycles (mid-year and year-end), with calibration by role family. Promotions are based on documented impact, demonstrated competencies, and manager + peer feedback.

Promotion process (summary):
1. Manager prepares promotion packet (impact examples, rubric mapping).
2. Packet reviewed in calibration meeting.
3. People Ops and comp approve band changes and equity adjustments.
4. Manager communicates outcome with development plan.

Growth support: mentors program, career ladder workshops, and the learning stipend.

## 9. Leaves, Time Off, and Flexible Work

- PTO: flexible policy; request through HR portal and notify manager ahead of time.
- Holidays: company-observed holidays are published annually.
- Parental and caregiver leave: follow local statutory rules plus Redwood top-up where applicable.
- Short-term disability and long-term disability: details in benefits portal.

## 10. FAQs and Contacts

Q: Who do I contact for payroll questions?
A: payroll@redwood.com (Finance).

Q: How do I request equipment?
A: Submit an IT ticket via the IT Service Portal (link in Slack #it-support).

Q: Where are security policies?
A: See confluence/security-and-compliance for audit, RBAC, and incident response docs.

Key contacts:
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
- IT & Desk Ops: it-support@redwood.com
- Benefits: benefits@redwood.com
- Recruiting: recruiting@redwood.com

## 11. Appendix: Templates and Links

- New hire 30/60/90 template (link)
- Offer letter template (People Ops internal)
- Manager 1:1 agenda template
- Career ladder rubrics per function (Engineering / Product / Research)

Document maintenance
- Owner: People Ops (owner_team).
- Review cadence: annual review, or sooner when benefits or policies change.
- For updates: open a PR on the handbook repo or email people-ops@redwood.com.

This handbook is intended to be the single source of truth for general employment questions. Team-level and role-specific processes may augment but not contradict this document.
